top_comments.text: From my experience coming from a mainly plant based diet my entire life, I think higher fat is the way to begin, but then gradually decrease as your body adjusts. Initially, it feeds your brain whereby years of lowfat eating left it nutritionally depleted. It keeps you satiated, while building healthy reserves and balancing hormones while you transition to burning your own fat as fuel. It might not work for everyone, but I think as you get more in tune with your body and hunger signals, you will naturally decrease fat anyway. There is no set time limit either. top_comments.text: I get what you are trying to say, but every animal on earth has a proper diet for their species, humans included. Can you tell me what the human requirement for carbohydrates is ? How about fiber ? I agree with you that a standard American diet or a vegan diet is bad, but there is no proof we need to eat any plants. Some people enjoy eating them, but that is a preference and nothing to do with human nutrition or health. Many civilizations ate grains, roots, fruit, and other plant foods because it was better than starving. Even the early American mountain men who explored the west for the first time, they found very little plants and fruit to eat, and nothing in the winter months.
